latest_published_issue.title: The Calm After the Storm
latest_published_issue.dek: Darkspaces sets a perfect lineup and still loses by 65.06 to CMac91's 183.42. The chat goes quiet, the block stays open, and ten games remain before the playoffs. Issue 5 covers Week 4 and previews Week 5.
ticker: Darkspaces sets a perfect 118.36 and loses by 65.06 to CMac91
Zygon beats Hades9mm and stays the lone unbeaten team
Swift, Collins and Pickens hit the block as the chat goes quiet
Painty69 loses by 1.34 and is the last winless team

Darkspaces.tagline: Commissioner, negotiator, and the owner of the 1.01.
file: The type
A commissioner who competes, and a competitor who negotiates in public. Every roster move comes with an audience.
Signature move
Naming a price in the chat, then renegotiating it live. Swift for next year's 1st, Collins on the block, and an Achane ask that started at a first.
Nemesis
The ceiling. A perfect lineup in Week 4 scored 118.36 and lost by 65.06 to CMac91.
The desk is watching
Whether a block full of receivers and backs becomes a trade before the deadline, and what is left of a FAAB budget that is down to $104.

2026.headline: A perfect lineup, a 65-point loss, and the 1.01
story: The draft set the tone. Darkspaces cut the pick timer to a minute, loaded up on receivers, and handed nicknames to twenty-three of his own players, then spent the first waiver run buying a tight end he had not drafted for $101 and Singleton for $301 on top of it. That is $402 gone before the first Monday night, and the wallet is down to $104.

The pattern since is spend big, sell high, talk loudly. Deebo Samuel went to Snipe58 for a 2027 2nd, Colston Loveland went for Jake Ferguson, and Matthew Stafford went to the same buyer for two future 2nds and $100 of FAAB. Week 4 brought no trade, only talk: Swift pitched to Painty69 and Sarge71 for next year's 1st, Nico Collins on the block, and Achane's knee in the chat.

The record is 2-2 after two wins and two losses. In Week 4 he set a perfect lineup, 118.36 with nothing left on the bench, and lost by 65.06 to CMac91. It was the lowest best-possible lineup of the week, which is how he holds the lowest MAXPF in the league and the 1.01. The desk will note that the commissioner wrote the MAXPF rule and is leading the race it created.
takes: Perfect process, no ceiling.
The negotiation is the content.

Snipe58.tagline: The quiet buyer with a very loud ledger.
file: The type
A win-now buyer who pays with the future. Stays out of the chat and lets the transaction log do the talking.
Signature move
Quietly converting picks into veterans. Deebo Samuel cost a 2027 2nd, Jake Ferguson cost Colston Loveland, and Matthew Stafford cost two future 2nds and $100 of FAAB.
Nemesis
Darkspaces, who is both his supplier and the commissioner who gets paid in picks every time he buys.
The desk is watching
Whether Stafford converts, because the roster is built around two quarterbacks and a .500 record.

2026.headline: Three trades, three veterans, and 2-2
story: Snipe58 does not post much, but the ledger is loud. In four weeks he has bought Deebo Samuel for a 2027 2nd, traded Loveland for Ferguson, and paid a 2028 2nd, a 2029 2nd and $100 of FAAB for Stafford. Each deal was a present-tense purchase funded with future capital.

The roster has the pieces. Justin Jefferson was the Week 1 MVP at 31.2, Brock Purdy was the Week 3 MVP at 31.28 and still lost to Johnny4Skins, and Quinshon Judkins led Week 4 at 21.6. With Stafford on the roster too, he has the dual-QB problem the desk has been writing about.

Week 4 was the win he needed: 112.22 over YesChef23 by 11.76, with 21.28 left on the bench. The record is 2-2, ninth in the standings, and the second-lowest MAXPF gives him the 1.02, which makes every future sell-off look reasonable and every buy look expensive.
takes: Buys the present, sells the future, and hopes the schedule notices.
Therapy is ongoing. Results pending.

StealingGas.tagline: The open tank with a conscience and a calendar.
file: The type
A self-declared tanker with a competitor's wallet. Announces the plan, then spends against it.
Signature move
The announcement-then-purchase combo: tank declared in Week 2, $99 on Stribling immediately, then $298 on Jaxson Dart.
Nemesis
Darkspaces and the public chat, plus Johnny4Skins, who beat him by 24.4 in Week 4.
The desk is watching
Whether he stays the 1.03 or pivots. In Week 4 he said he may throw away all his capital to catch Hades9mm and Zygon, though it may end poorly. FAAB is down to $98.

2026.headline: 1-3, the 1.03, and a pivot on the table
story: StealingGas opened the year with the league's worst score at 83.32, repeated it with 77.18 in Week 2, and announced the tank. Then he spent $99 on a waiver dart, followed it with $298 on Jaxson Dart, and in Week 3 posted a perfect 152.42 lineup to beat Darkspaces by 83. Week 4 brought a 133.5 loss to Johnny4Skins and a 1-3 record.

He is also the league's most active seller of his own roster. The London deal with Hades9mm was the real move: he took Drake London, Taylen Green and a 2027 1st, and sent Quentin Johnston, Cam Ward, TreVeyon Henderson and a 2027 3rd the other way. Week 4 was small change: Sampson and Kendre Miller from free agency, and Eli Raridon for $1 in place of Kyler Murray.

The chat bits stay reliable and the box scores stay confusing. His 446.42 points are the lowest in the league, and his MAXPF is the third-lowest, which keeps the 1.03 in reach. Then he told the chat he would see how the team looks in a few weeks, and that a pivot may end poorly for him. The desk is taking notes.
takes: The tank is real, the box scores disagree.
See you in 2028, with a $298 receipt.

Zygon.tagline: The IR Predictor. The formula does not miss.
file: The type
The algorithm manager. Builds the roster around production, then lets the numbers run.
Signature move
Listing handcuffs on the block as a dare. Emmett Johnson and Blake Corum are posted with the line make me regret it when Walker tears his ACL.
Nemesis
Health. The team name is a prediction and Kenneth Walker and Mahomes are on the roster. Nobody else can hurt this team.
The desk is watching
Whether a $5 bid on Jacoby Brissett is insurance or a leak in the formula, and the Week 5 Match of the Week against C33DeezNutzz.

2026.headline: 4-0, the biggest bid yet, and the nickname still cashing
story: Zygon is the only team in the league that is unbeaten, and the only one that has barely touched the waiver wire. His FAAB spend is $7: $2 on Ollie Gordon and, in Week 4, $5 on Jacoby Brissett. The team is 4-0 with the league's highest points total, built on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Kenneth Walker and Patrick Mahomes.

The scores back it up. 195.70 in Week 1, a 172.96 in Week 2 that beat YesChef23 by 92.86 and earned Best Manager, 149.78 in Week 3 over Sarge71, and 144.02 in Week 4 over Hades9mm. Walker led the Match of the Week at 30.9, though Javonte Williams on the other side scored 31.3, so Zygon won on depth, not on one star.

The desk's complaint is that the formula is hard to write around. Zygon left 36.08 on the bench and still won by 22.26, swapped Detroit for the Chicago Bears defense, and kept the handcuffs on the block. The 1.11 slot says his best-case lineup is one of the league's strongest. Next up is C33DeezNutzz, the cleanest lineup manager on the board.
takes: The formula does not bid on anyone. Until it does.
Elite bit commitment: the injury nickname, the 4-0, and the win.

Hades9mm.tagline: The sleeper puss, fully awake, with a first loss.
file: The type
A balanced, hand-built roster and a buyer's budget. Every one of his 23 picks was his own, which is the rarest thing in this league.
Signature move
Selling a star for depth. The London deal moved Drake London for Quentin Johnston, Cam Ward, TreVeyon Henderson and a 2027 3rd.
Nemesis
Zygon, who beat him in the Week 4 Match of the Week, and Darkspaces, the other half of the files feud.
The desk is watching
The 12th draft slot, the highest MAXPF in the league at 764.18, and the 29.1 left on the bench in Week 4.

2026.headline: 3-1 without London, and the first loss came against the leader
story: Hades9mm drafted every one of his 23 picks himself, and the roster shows it: Jayden Daniels and Jared Goff at quarterback, Amon-Ra St. Brown and London at receiver, Derrick Henry and Cam Skattebo at running back, Kittle and Kelce at tight end. He started 3-0 with 186.00, 169.62 and 139.80, then lost 144.02 to 121.76 against Zygon in Week 4. He is second in the standings and in points.

The money is the story. He spent $170 of FAAB in a single week on Benson and Gesicki, then traded London in the deal with StealingGas that Sleeper logged in Week 2, took a bag of young players and a 2027 3rd, and was quiet on the wire in Week 4. His FAAB is $330.

The files feud with Darkspaces is his best content. He laid out the opening ask himself, four 1sts for Darkspaces' Mendoza, Maye, Achane and Egbuka, then threatened to release the trade-talk logs. The desk's view: the best lineup on the board still leaves points on the bench, and the schedule has been kind. Painty69 is next, which will not hurt.
takes: The sleeper puss is no longer sleeping, and just spent like it.
3-1 without London. Either the deal was fine or the schedule is soft.

file: The type
The league's most hands-off roster. Johnny4Skins drafted a few good players, then left the room and let the system finish the job.
Signature move
Not spending. Zero FAAB used, $500 intact, and the roster is the same one the autopick built.
Nemesis
Injuries to either quarterback, and Zygon, who beat him by 70 in Week 1.
The desk is watching
Darkspaces in Week 5, and the dual-QB gamble: Lamar Jackson at 2.04 and Jalen Hurts auto-drafted at 3.04.

2026.headline: Eighteen autopicks, $500 untouched, 3-1
story: Johnny4Skins took Ja'Marr Chase and Lamar Jackson in the first two rounds, then, apparently, went to dinner. The autopick drafted eighteen of his players, tied with Painty69 for the most in the league, including Jalen Hurts, A.J. Brown, Tyler Warren, Kyren Williams, Brian Thomas and DK Metcalf. Not a single human opinion went into any of them.

It keeps working. He lost to Zygon in Week 1, beat Painty69 in Week 2, posted 158.46 over Snipe58 in Week 3, and in Week 4 scored 157.9 over StealingGas with Kyren Williams at 36.7, leaving 24.5 on the bench. He is 3-1, third in the standings, and the $500 of FAAB is untouched, which the desk now treats as an identity.

The roster is dual-QB by design or by accident. The honest answer is that it does not matter until an injury forces a decision. He also has a new handle: the account was Cassellrole until October. Next up: Darkspaces.
takes: The robot spent nothing.
A good autopick is still not a plan.

Sarge71.tagline: The engine without the supporting cast, finally with a win.
file: The type
A top-end roster with nothing underneath. Star power at running back, and a bench that cannot cover a bye week.
Signature move
The quiet transaction. One move this season, cutting Jaxson Dart, watching StealingGas pay $298 for him, and taking Aaron Rodgers instead.
Nemesis
The schedule. His 635.08 points against are the most in the league.
The desk is watching
Whether the roster adds one real depth piece, and the 53.52 points he left on the bench in Week 4.

2026.headline: A win with the week's worst lineup
story: Sarge71 started 0-3 with points that would win in a weaker schedule: 145.00 in Week 1, which lost to C33DeezNutzz's 195.82, 110.60 in Week 2 and 117.88 in Week 3. Week 4 finally broke the streak, 134.66 to 133.32 over Painty69 by 1.34. His points against are the highest in the league at 635.08.

The roster is Bijan Robinson and a supporting cast that is finally scoring. Tetairoa McMillan went for 45.2 in Week 4, the best score of any player in the issue, on top of Robinson's Week 1 MVP at 31.3 and Week 3 MVP at 35.3. He cut Jaxson Dart, watched StealingGas bid $298 on him, and replaced him with Aaron Rodgers.

He also set the worst lineup of the week, 72% of a perfect one per Sleeper's report, and won anyway. At 1-3 he is 10th in the standings and holds the 1.05. FAAB is untouched at $500, and the more useful move is still a trade, which Sarge71 has not made.
takes: Sarge has the engine and, sometimes, a cast.
A very good score wins most weeks. A bad lineup won this one.

C33DeezNutzz.tagline: The efficient one. BBQnBBWs does not waste points.
file: The type
A quiet, efficient contender. Cleanest lineup management on the board, and only 14.3 left on the bench in Week 4.
Signature move
The workmanlike win. Josh Allen as the engine and a steady lineup behind him.
Nemesis
Hades9mm, who beat him in Week 2, and fumbduckdumbfuck, who beat him by 12.1 in Week 4.
The desk is watching
Zygon in the Match of the Week, and FAAB, which is untouched at $500.

2026.headline: 2-2, the cleanest lineup, and the Zygon test
story: C33DeezNutzz opened with a 195.82, the highest score of Week 1, with Josh Allen providing 35.66, then lost to Hades9mm in Week 2 despite 40.82 from Allen, then beat CMac91 in Week 3 with a workmanlike 127.90. In Week 4 he lost 133.88 to 121.78 against fumbduckdumbfuck, with Zay Flowers leading at 25.8.

The roster is a Josh Allen core with Justin Herbert, Chris Olave, Ladd McConkey and Bucky Irving around him, and the waiver activity is minimal. His FAAB is a full $500, and the desk keeps asking when it becomes a weapon.

He is 2-2, fourth in the standings, third in points, and picks 6th on MAXPF. The cleanest lineup in the league just lost to a roster that left 30.4 on the bench, which is football. Zygon is next, and a win would be the best argument for process over volume.
takes: Not a fireworks card. Just a workmanlike manager.
Quiet is not the same as safe, but it is close.

Painty69.tagline: Elite top end, a robot bottom, and a promise to be kind.
file: The type
A star at running back and almost nothing else. Made his last real pick in round 6 and let the CPU draft the remaining seventeen rounds.
Signature move
The positive attitude. He promised to be positive and kind through the whole draft and has been quiet since Week 2.
Nemesis
YesChef23, who needles him in the restaurant arc, and Sarge71, who beat him by 1.34 in Week 4.
The desk is watching
Hades9mm in Week 5, and whether Gibbs gets a second scorer before the 0-4 hardens.

2026.headline: 0-4 by 1.34, and the league's last winless team
story: Painty69 took Jahmyr Gibbs at 1.01, then McCaffrey and Barkley back to back, and then stopped. The last real pick was in round 6, and the CPU made the remaining seventeen, tying him with Johnny4Skins at eighteen autopicks. The feed has since shown him moving Sarratt, Aiyuk and Klubnik, three of the robot's choices.

He is 0-4 with 497.14 points. The losses were by 12.7, 32.3, 4.7 and now 1.34 to Sarge71, with Joe Burrow leading Week 4 at 25.72 and 46.0 points left on the bench. Gibbs has been excellent, but Week 4 shows the problem: even a good lineup loses when the bench is carrying more than the margin.

The silence is the other story. Four of the five votes in the Issue 4 poll said he stays in the bottom three, and he did not say a word in this log. The rivalry with YesChef23 gave the restaurant arc a result, but the desk's view is simpler: a top-end roster with a robot bottom, and a manager who left in the middle. He picks 7th on MAXPF.
takes: Gibbs did his job. Everyone else did not.
Positive and kind, right up until the robot took over.

CMac91.tagline: The depth collector who finally went off.
file: The type
The league's most patient manager. Builds depth, stays out of drama, and has not spent a dollar of FAAB.
Signature move
Adding depth at no cost. Jaydon Blue, Travis Hunter and Kimani Vidal arrived without a bid.
Nemesis
Hades9mm, who beat him by 53 in Week 1, and C33DeezNutzz, who beat him by 9 in Week 3.
The desk is watching
Whether 183.42 was a breakout or a spike, and fumbduckdumbfuck in Week 5.

2026.headline: 183.42, three spots up, zero dollars spent
story: CMac91 asked in round 5 whether there were seriously 23 rounds, played through round 11, and let the robot finish the draft, which gave him twelve autopicks. The first-round pick was James Cook, followed by CeeDee Lamb at 2.02 and Bo Nix at 3.02.

Lamb has been the engine. He provided the Week 2 MVP at 35.3 and the Week 4 MVP at 41.3, in a 183.42 to 118.36 win over Darkspaces by 65.06, the high score of the week and the biggest margin. Only 5.52 sat on the bench. The earlier losses were to Hades9mm in Week 1 and C33DeezNutzz in Week 3, by 53 and by 9.

The wire is still his comfort zone, and the FAAB is a full $500. At 2-2 he jumped three spots to 5th, with 564.98 points and the 9th pick on MAXPF. In the hat saga his contribution was closing the matter with it works. That sums up the approach.
takes: Depth first, spending never.
It works.

YesChef23.tagline: The restaurant arc. Wins ugly, complains loudly. Lost ugly this time.
file: The type
A chef who wins while complaining. Chatty in the draft room, aggressive on waivers, and 2-2 with the lowest score of the week.
Signature move
Cheap waiver insurance. $1 on Deshaun Watson when Caleb Williams went down, $1 on J.J. McCarthy the week after, and in Week 4 $12 on Keon Coleman.
Nemesis
Painty69, who he has needled since the draft room, and Snipe58, who beat him by 11.76 in Week 4.
The desk is watching
The receiver room: Coleman, Roman Wilson and Joe Mixon are new, George Pickens is on the block, and 38.2 points sat on the bench in Week 4.

2026.headline: The lowest score of the week and a wire full of new names
story: YesChef23 opened the draft fighting an Uber Eats driver who stole a customer's order, took shots at the turtle ass drafters, and threatened to take defenses the rest of the way before settling for two. He beat fumbduckdumbfuck in Week 1, lost to Zygon by 92.86 in Week 2, and beat Painty69 in Week 3 by 4.68.

The roster is built on Caleb Williams and Jeremiyah Love, and when Williams went down he paid $1 for Deshaun Watson and then $1 for J.J. McCarthy. In Week 4 he made three claims for $14: Coleman at $12, Wilson at $1 and Mixon at $1. Coleman had just been dropped by Darkspaces. Then he listed George Pickens.

The week went badly. 100.46 was the lowest score of the week, he left 38.2 on the bench, and Snipe58 beat him by 11.76. He is 2-2, down three spots to 8th, with 456.18 points and the 4th pick on MAXPF. The wire is still the roster.
takes: Wins ugly, complains loudly.
The cheapest insurance policy in the league, until the $12 bid.

file: The type
The desk's preseason favorite, and a roster that is better than the record. Fifth-best in points, sixth in the standings.
Signature move
Quietly good at running back. Jeanty, Taylor and Bowers form a core that scores every week.
Nemesis
YesChef23, who ended the Issue 1 No. 1 label in Week 1, and Hades9mm, who beat him by 12 in Week 3.
The desk is watching
The quarterback room. Kyler Murray arrived free in Week 4 in place of Kayshon Boutte.

2026.headline: Back to 2-2 and still searching for a quarterback
story: fumbduckdumbfuck was the desk's number one in Issue 1, and the roster still supports it: Brock Bowers at 1.12, Ashton Jeanty at 2.01, Jonathan Taylor at 3.01, with Rashee Rice, DeVonta Smith and Dak Prescott behind them. He is 2-2 with 530.88 points and sits 6th, up one spot.

The losses were close. 113.10 to 127.06 against YesChef23 in Week 1, and 127.74 to 139.80 against Hades9mm in Week 3. The wins were a 156.16 to 110.60 beat-down of Sarge71 in Week 2 and a 133.88 to 121.78 win over C33DeezNutzz in Week 4, with Taylor leading at 22.7, despite 30.4 points on the bench.

The quarterback room is the open question. Aaron Rodgers arrived as an autopick, was moved to free agency, and the Week 3 move was a swap involving Drew Lock and Geno Smith. Week 4 brought Kyler Murray, cut by StealingGas earlier in the week, for Boutte. The 8th pick on MAXPF says the roster has a good best case, and the record says it is finally being realized.
takes: Jonathan Taylor did the real work.
The Issue 1 No. 1 label is a lot to carry, but it is lighter at 2-2.

desk: The storm passed. Draft hype and early-season noise carried the league through four weeks, and Week 4 arrived with a thin chat log, a scoreboard doing most of the talking, and ten games left before the playoffs. Teams are still searching for an identity, and the block shows it: Darkspaces listed Nico Collins and pitched Swift for a first, and YesChef23 posted George Pickens. No trade cleared this week. The deadline will change that.

On the field, Darkspaces set a perfect lineup, 118.36 with nothing left on the bench, and lost by 65.06 to CMac91's 183.42, the high score of the week. A perfect lineup is only as good as the roster behind it, and MAXPF, the points of each week's best possible lineup added up, now gives Darkspaces the league's lowest total and the 1.01. Zygon beat Hades9mm and is the only unbeaten team. Painty69 lost by 1.34 and is the only winless one.

paras: Week 4 was the calm after the storm. The draft hype and the early scramble have burned off, the first third of the regular season is behind us, and most teams are still working out what they are. Ten games remain before the playoffs, and the urge to trade grows every week the block stays open.

The field is clearer than the chat. Zygon is the only 4-0 team, Hades9mm and Johnny4Skins sit at 3-1, six teams are bunched at 2-2, and Painty69 is the lone 0-4. Darkspaces holds the 1.01 on MAXPF, Snipe58 the 1.02 and StealingGas the 1.03, which keeps the tank math alive.

Issue 4's poll went four votes to Painty69 staying in the bottom three, one to Sarge71, and none for StealingGas or the field. Next up: Zygon vs C33DeezNutzz for the unbeaten crown, Darkspaces needing a bounce-back against Johnny4Skins, and a new poll below. Cast your vote, then go start somebody.
